We have target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need propose retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions. The hints: step1: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So likely disconnection: break sulfonamide bond between aniline (first phenyl with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So precursor1: p-toluidine (or methyl phenyl amine) with sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthetic step: target -> split into amine (the aniline part) and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So we need to identify the amine: the part "Cc1ccc(N... )cc1" is an aniline with methyl. So precursor A: 4-methylaniline (p-toluidine) SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1. Precursor B: aryl sulfonyl chloride: the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl with the rest of chain. The sulfonyl chloride would be "ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2". So step1: sulfonamide formation.

Step2: amide formation: the chain "/C=C/C(=O)N..." is an amide formed from carboxylic acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid (alpha,beta-unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline). The acid is "C=C-COOH attached to phenyl sulfonyl phenyl". Actually the acid is "c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2" after removing amide N? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline. So precursor acid: the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl phenyl: "c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2" with sulfonyl group attached to that phenyl. So we need to have that acid (maybe from Doebner modification). The amine is aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step2: amide coupling.

Step3: Doebner modification to form the alpha,beta-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. The aldehyde would be the aromatic aldehyde on the phenyl ring (the same phenyl that later becomes the sulfonyl phenyl). The aldehyde is "c2ccc(C=O)cc2" with sulfonyl group attached? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl at position where the aldehyde is? In target, the sulfonyl phenyl has the side chain at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl phenyl has the side chain at para position (maybe). So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl with sulfonyl group and aldehyde at para position: "ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2"? Wait sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl, not aldehyde. The aldehyde is on that phenyl after sulfonyl? Actually the side chain attaches to phenyl via the double bond: /C=C/. So the aldehyde would be "c2ccc(C=O)cc2" with sulfonyl group attached at the same carbon as the aldehyde? The sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl at the position where the side chain attaches? In target, the sulfonyl phenyl is attached to the side chain via the phenyl carbon (the phenyl is attached to the sulfonyl group, not to the side chain). The side chain attaches to the phenyl at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl attaches to phenyl at position 1, the side chain attaches at position 4 (para). So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl with sulfonyl group and aldehyde at para position: "ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2". Then Doebner modification with malonic acid yields the unsaturated acid with side chain (C=C-COOH). So step3: Doebner modification.

Thus we have three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation, 2) amide coupling, 3) Doebner modification.

Now we need to construct JSON route: root molecule target, children reaction nodes each with template_id. Need template IDs for each step. We have template ID 733 for sulfonamide formation (found earlier). For amide coupling, we need a template that forms amide from carboxylic acid and amine. Could search.
